judged_text: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb is not idempotent and the UI invites re-submission: there is no existing-membership check before group.add(user), the usernames input is not cleared after adding, and the button isn't disabled during the request, so re-adding the same member either creates duplicate GroupUser rows (member listed twice, user_count inflated) or raises a unique-constraint error → 500 that is swallowed client-side; the old PUT flow (usernames= setter) reconciled the set and avoided this

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` blindly calls `group.add(user)` for each username without any explicit existing-membership check, and the new UI action `addMembers` has a `// TODO: should clear the input` plus no request-in-flight disabling (admin-group.js.es6). However, the claim that this will *definitely* create duplicate GroupUser rows, inflate `user_count`, or raise a unique-constraint 500 cannot be verified from the diff because the behavior/constraints of `Group#add` / the join model aren’t shown. So the concrete, diff-grounded issue is an idempotence/UX robustness concern rather than a provable defect.
